intro.data: Here's a different functor: Optional wraps each type in "maybe." A functor isn't a free-for-all relabeling — follow the arrows so every step still connects. Map the chain.
intro.alchemy: Here's a different functor: Trace wraps each material in "a trace of." A functor isn't a free relabeling — follow the arrows so every step still connects. Map the chain.
intro.spellcraft: Here's a different functor: Echo wraps each essence in "a whisper of." A functor isn't a free relabeling — follow the arrows so every step still connects. Map the chain.
intro.abstract: Here's a different functor G. A functor isn't a free relabeling — every source arrow must land on a target arrow with matching ends. Map the chain.

goal.data: Map the chain A → B → C onto its Optional version so both steps still connect.
goal.alchemy: Map the chain A → B → C onto its Trace version so both steps still connect.
goal.spellcraft: Map the chain A → B → C onto its Echo version so both steps still connect.
goal.abstract: Map A, B, C and f, g so every arrow's endpoints are preserved.

afterSuccess.data: Because each arrow's ends are fixed, the objects can only line up one way. Swap the middle and a step would have nowhere to land. Optional is just as much a functor as List — there can be many.
afterSuccess.alchemy: Because each arrow's ends are fixed, the objects can only line up one way. Swap the middle and a step would have nowhere to land. Trace is just as much a functor as Bundle.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: Because each arrow's ends are fixed, the objects can only line up one way. Swap the middle and a step would have nowhere to land. Echo is just as much a functor as Set.
afterSuccess.abstract: Because each arrow's ends are fixed, the objects can only line up one way. A functor must respect every arrow — and many different functors can exist between the same two categories.

reveal.summary: A functor must preserve every arrow's source and target, so the object and morphism assignments have to agree. Different functors (List, Optional, …) give different — but all valid — maps.
reveal.moreFormal: There is usually more than one functor C → D. Each is a complete, structure-preserving copy of C inside D; the identity functor and constant functors are always available too.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: Both List and Optional are functors with their own map; you pick which world to map into.
